consequence.statement: The operator must update the Flux CLI to the latest release (via a package manager or the binary from GitHub releases) and verify with `flux --version`; without this step the environment keeps running an outdated Flux CLI.
consequence.remediation: Update the Flux CLI to the latest release using a package manager or by downloading the binary from GitHub releases, then verify with `flux --version`.

original.statement: The Flux 2.7.0 upgrade guide instructs operators to update the Flux CLI to the latest release, using `flux check --pre` to detect whether a newer Flux version is available and `flux --version` to verify the running version.

decision.reason: [ev-2d6ff80d75f9] is the whole "Flux CLI upgrade" section of the upgrade guide. It is general how-to text: run `flux check --pre`, update the CLI, then check with `flux --version`. It does not say that anything fails, is rejected or stops being honoured if the operator skips the CLI update, so migration-required claims mandatory work the evidence does not support. Because the text names no product change and no consequence, no corrected assertion follows from it, and "none" would also be a guess.
